clue.text: Get singer rocking in "Hello"

indicators.note: something rocking is shaken about, so the letters before it are tossed into a new order

parts.note: the two words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A vocalist launches into a rock version of the song "Hello".
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks dress Hello up as a song title; it is simply the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Greetings is said as an interjection of welcome, the same job a cheery hello does.

clue.text: Some lift heavy article

indicators.note: some of the following words means only a part of their letters is taken

parts.note: the end of lift runs into the start of heavy

explanation.surface: Raising a weighty item off the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the definite article is the commonest instance of the word class called articles.

clue.text: Notice boy going round vehicle after parking

indicators.note: after tells us the parking letter comes first and the rest follows it

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

indicators.note: going round means the boy word encircles the vehicle word

parts.note: a lad is a boy
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A boy circles his car in a car park after spotting a sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A placard is a public sign or poster displayed so people will see it, a kind of written notice.

clue.text: Fine applications programming interface for browser

parts.note: OK means fine, all right
the standard initialism for an application programming interface

explanation.surface: Praise for a software interface that suits a web browser.
explanation.walkthrough: The computing words make browser look like web software; here it is an animal that browses, feeding on leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi, a forest relative of the giraffe, feeds by stripping leaves from trees, which zoologists call browsing.

clue.text: In good alloys furiously checks everything's ready

indicators.note: In places the good letter inside the rearranged material
doing something furiously means wildly and chaotically, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
taken as written, to be rearranged
to stem a flow is to check it; also rearranged

explanation.surface: Metal testing in a foundry finds everything satisfactory.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of alloys and stems make ALLSYSTEMSO, and G slips in before the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from rocket launches, where controllers announce that every component is prepared and the mission may proceed.

clue.text: Not to make oneself read fiction initially is backward

definitions.note: a preposition defined by its opposite

indicators.note: backward means the selected letters are read in the opposite direction
initially points to the opening letter of each of the words just before it

parts.note: the opening letters of those four words

explanation.surface: A reluctant reader refuses to force themselves through novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Prepositions of direction pair off as opposites: one marks a starting point, the other the destination.

clue.text: Figure seen in Piccadilly tea rooms regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, every second one here

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A tourist spots a statue while taking tea in central London.
explanation.walkthrough: The winged statue atop the Shaftesbury Memorial Fountain in Piccadilly Circus, London, is popularly called Eros.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous statue at Piccadilly Circus in London is universally known by the name of the Greek love god.

clue.text: Women's regatta team raise Royal sportsperson

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
a rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen
to lift is to raise
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher

explanation.surface: A women's rowing crew hoists a royal athlete onto their shoulders.
explanation.walkthrough: A regatta is a rowing race meeting, and its standard crew is an eight.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor who hoists barbells in an Olympic strength discipline is an athlete, a sportsperson.

clue.text: Welshman involved in unsteady landing

indicators.note: involved in means caught up inside the following words, not built from outside them

parts.note: found across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A man from Wales takes part in a wobbly touchdown.
explanation.walkthrough: Dylan is a classic Welsh name, as borne by the poet Dylan Thomas.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is distinctively Welsh, borne most famously by the poet Thomas from Swansea.

clue.text: Extra box located in boot?

indicators.note: located in places the box word inside the boot word

parts.note: the toe is the front part of a boot; the question mark flags this part-for-whole hint
to spar is to box

explanation.surface: A surplus item stashed in a car boot, perhaps a spare wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: A car boot is the trunk, which makes a spare tyre spring to mind; but the boot is footwear, and its toe holds the boxing word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left over beyond what is needed is extra, as in having time or money left over.

clue.text: Novel's understood when read aloud

indicators.note: when read aloud means we take the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: understood means knew, which is said exactly like the answer

explanation.surface: A book's meaning becomes clear once you read it out.
explanation.walkthrough: Novel looks like a book, but here it is the adjective meaning fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Novel as an adjective means original and not seen before, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Go over and promise to produce this

parts.note: to cross a road is to go over it
giving your word is promising

explanation.surface: An instruction for making the very puzzle you are solving.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points at the puzzle itself, a common self-referential joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The thing in front of the solver is a grid of interlocking clued words, so the pronoun stands for it.

clue.text: Grand parrot making one stare

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
to parrot is to copy or mimic, to ape

explanation.surface: A magnificent parrot is so striking that onlookers gawp.
explanation.walkthrough: Parrot looks like the bird but is the verb meaning to imitate.
explanation.definitionFit: To gape is to look wide-eyed with the mouth open, gazing in wonder, which is staring.

clue.text: Authorizer's been crazily associated with brief lark

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter is dropped
crazily signals letters jumbled into a wild new order

parts.note: taken as written
lark without its final letter

explanation.surface: An official who approves things has been mixed up in a silly prank.
explanation.definitionFit: One who empowers or gives permission for something to happen makes it possible, so authorizes it.

clue.text: Leaves note with answer

definitions.note: plural noun for a mass noun

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: Someone departs, leaving a note with a reply.
explanation.walkthrough: Leaves reads as a verb, someone departing; it is the noun, dried plant leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: The drink is brewed from the dried foliage of the Camellia plant, sold loose as tea leaves.

clue.text: CID officer's grabbed by lunatic: streaker?

indicators.note: grabbed by means held inside the word that follows

parts.note: a nut is a crazy person
a DI is a Detective Inspector in the CID, with the possessive s

explanation.surface: A detective is seized by a madman who runs naked across the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is Britain's Criminal Investigation Department, the plain-clothes detective branch of the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A streaker runs naked in public, and someone who goes without clothes is, at least for the moment, a naturist.

clue.text: Notes bad coffee not cold — but in a sense completely defective

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters are spoilt and so put into the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: not cold means the letter standing for cold is removed

parts.note: decaf is decaffeinated coffee; C for cold comes out

explanation.surface: A complaint about dreadful coffee that has gone cold.
explanation.walkthrough: C is the tap abbreviation for cold, so DECAF loses C to make DEAF.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearing is one of the senses, and being totally unable to hear is a complete failure of that one faculty.

clue.text: Thursday, when consuming water initially, gets more cordial?

parts.note: TH is a short form of Thursday

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing up, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A weekday on which drinking water makes people friendlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who becomes less frosty and more friendly is figuratively melting, as ice does when warmed.

clue.text: Energy and nonsense: I'd upset press person

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the words before it read upwards

parts.note: rot means nonsense
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A journalist claims the press is all energy and rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers are collectively the press, and the person who runs a newspaper is one of its people.

clue.text: Chopin's my sort of composition!

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; the clue treats it as describing a kind of composition

indicators.note: a sort of something is a version of it, so the letters are sorted into a fresh order

parts.note: these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A music lover declares Chopin's work is just their kind of music.
explanation.walkthrough: Chopin wrote no symphonies, which adds a wink to the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Symphonic describes music in the form of a symphony, a large orchestral work and type of composition.

clue.text: Herb ducks hugging ungrateful daughter

indicators.note: hugging means wrapping around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, looking like O
Regan is one of King Lear's ungrateful daughters in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: Waterbirds cuddle a thankless girl near the herb garden.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, so ducks are two Os.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is a Mediterranean culinary plant of the mint family, used dried as a seasoning herb.

clue.text: Old nurse has got married in the country

indicators.note: has got means holds within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: SEN, State Enrolled Nurse, was a former British nursing grade
wed means married

explanation.surface: A retired nurse has married and moved out to the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The country looks like rural parts; it is a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweden is a Scandinavian nation, so it is a country in the political sense, not the rural one.

clue.text: Very drunk: stain on part of bible turning up

parts.note: a blot is a stain

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is part of the Bible

explanation.surface: A mark appears on a page of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is informal British slang for being extremely intoxicated, as drunk as can be.

clue.text: Relative the opposite of what Robin Hood was?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a relation by marriage

definitions.text: the opposite of what Robin Hood was
definitions.meaning: second meaning: Robin Hood was an outlaw, and in is the opposite of out

explanation.walkthrough: Robin Hood was the legendary English outlaw; swap out for in to get the playful second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation gained through marriage, such as a spouse's parent, is a relative of a kind.

clue.text: You and me and Lord join together

parts.note: you and I together are we
LD is the abbreviation for Lord

explanation.surface: Two people and a nobleman form an alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: To weld is to fuse metal pieces by heating, and more loosely to unite things firmly.

clue.text: Girl in family service supplying agents

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the Secret Intelligence Service, Britain's foreign spy agency also known as MI6

explanation.walkthrough: SIS is the Secret Intelligence Service, better known as MI6, which runs Britain's overseas spies.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal speech shortens sister for a female sibling, while the initials name Britain's spy service.
